scope: attempted same-operator two-host generation-anchor/witness probe; no live protocol result established

setup_observations.observation: A narrow Git fetch on neontic did not create the expected remote-tracking ref.
setup_observations.remediation: Used an explicit refspec and verified exact candidate b3846ac710676b63783eb356cde8558e3a2cff5f.

setup_observations.observation: NeonPC system Python and the QA virtual environment did not contain cryptography.
setup_observations.remediation: Used Git for Windows bundled OpenSSL 3.5.9 to generate ephemeral anchor TLS material without installing a new package.

setup_observations.observation: Generation-anchor HTTPS service started on NeonPC port 4447 with a fresh empty generation store.
RemoteGenerationAnchorClient on neontic returned no generation value. Direct verified-TLS diagnosis failed before TLS with PermissionError WinError 10013.
NeonPC Ethernet was Public while the first temporary inbound rule was Private-profile only.
setup_observations.remediation: Replaced the temporary rule with Profile Any while retaining exact source restriction 192.168.1.64 and TCP port 4447.

setup_observations.observation: The corrected firewall rule did not restore connectivity. Test-NetConnection to 192.168.1.81:4447 remained false and Python still returned WinError 10013.
Test-NetConnection from neontic to NeonPC Tailscale address 100.107.237.63:4447 also failed/timed out.

limitations: The failed route is an environment/network limitation, not evidence that the generation-floor protocol is incorrect.
No live witness-to-anchor read succeeded, so no live anti-rollback claim may be made from this attempt.
Only two operator-controlled machines were online; even a successful retry would not establish independent custody or three-party validation.
Synthetic and hosted tests remain the current evidence for witness-only rollback resistance and coordinated rollback vulnerability.
